top_story: A year after the ceasefire, Gaza has shifted from acute wartime destruction into entrenched social collapse, with no meaningful reconstruction, weak governance, and a health system still failing under restricted aid and delayed medical evacuations. Hunger and malnutrition have deepened this decay, forcing families to depend on scarce community kitchens and turning survival into a daily contest that compounds public despair. Against that backdrop, the exposure on 9 October of a Flydubai co-pilot’s alleged plan to carry out a suicide attack at Ben Gurion airport underscores how the unresolved Israeli-Palestinian crisis continues to radiate outward into regional security channels once seen as relatively insulated. The combined picture is of a conflict environment that is no longer defined only by front lines, but by the steady normalization of humanitarian ruin and the diffusion of extremist risk across civilian systems.
